+# 11. A Flix language module (`rewrite-flix`)
+
+Date: 2026-07-24
+
+## Status
+
+Proposed
+
+The decision to build the module, and to integrate via a **slim parser artifact** from the
+vendor pipeline (§ "How the Flix parser is obtained"), is accepted. A local spike
+(2026-07-24) has settled the production mechanism: **A1 source decoupling** (so the parser
+runs without a `Flix` instance) **+ R8 method-level shrinking + shading** — verified end to
+end (32 MB → 3.4 MB, parser round-trips); see "Spike results". What remains is applying A1 as a PR on the fork, wiring A2/shading into the vendor
+build, and starting `rewrite-flix`. No `rewrite-flix` code exists yet — this ADR records the
+checked feasibility findings and
+the plan so the work starts from facts rather than assumptions.
+
+## Context
+
+OpenRewrite has no support for [Flix](https://flix.dev), a JVM-based, Apache-2.0
+**functional** language with first-class effects, traits (type classes), enums, modules,
+and Datalog-style logic/fixpoint constructs. Flix has **no object-oriented model** — no
+classes, inheritance, or `this`-bound methods — so, unlike Scala, there is no OOP surface
+to map onto `rewrite-java`'s class-based `J.*` nodes. This ADR records whether and how a
+`rewrite-flix` module can
+be built to the same standard as the existing language modules, and settles the one
+decision that gates all coding: **how the Flix parser is obtained and run.**
+
+Every claim below was verified against the working tree or upstream Flix source; earlier
+informal analysis of this idea contained specifics that were not checked, and this ADR
+supersedes it.
+
+### The closest local model is `rewrite-scala`
+
+Flix is a Scala-implemented JVM language, and the nearest precedent in this repository is
+`rewrite-scala`, which sets the quality bar and the shape a Flix module should follow:
+
+* Its parser enforces **parse → print byte equality** — `ScalaParser.parseInputs`
+  finishes each source through `requirePrintEqualsInput(...)`
+  ([`ScalaParser.java:150`](../../rewrite-scala/src/main/java/org/openrewrite/scala/ScalaParser.java)),
+  so a parsed-then-printed source must reproduce its input exactly.
+* Its compilation unit selects the language printer directly —
+  `S.CompilationUnit.printer(...)` returns `new ScalaPrinter<>()`
+  ([`S.java`](../../rewrite-scala/src/main/java/org/openrewrite/scala/tree/S.java)).
+* The module is **large**: a 2,171-line `ScalaPrinter`, 62 test classes, ~25 Scala-specific
+  markers, a Scala-language compiler bridge (`ScalaCompilerBridge`, `ScalaASTConverter`,
+  `ScalaTypeMapping`, `ScalaTypeSignatureBuilder`), and format/style/service layers. It
+  reuses `J.*` from `rewrite-java` where valid and adds `S.*` nodes and markers for
+  Scala-only constructs, in line with
+  [ADR 5 (parser/LST conventions)](0005-parser-lst-conventions.md).
+
+A Flix module is a comparable multi-month effort, not a single change.
+
+### Feasibility findings (verified against Flix source)
+
+1. **There is a self-contained front-end to hook into.** Flix parses in phases —
+   [`Lexer`](https://github.com/wstein/flix-fork/blob/HEAD/main/src/ca/uwaterloo/flix/language/phase/Lexer.scala)
+   produces tokens, then the LL parser
+   [`Parser2`](https://github.com/wstein/flix-fork/blob/HEAD/main/src/ca/uwaterloo/flix/language/phase/Parser2.scala)
+   produces a `SyntaxTree`, then `Weeder2` desugars it into `WeededAst`. The LST is built
+   from the `SyntaxTree` — **after `Parser2`, before `Weeder2`** — so no desugaring is
+   lost. `Parser2`'s entry point is:
+
+   ```scala
+   def run(tokens0: Map[Source, Array[Token]], oldRoot: SyntaxTree.Root, changeSet: ChangeSet)
+          (implicit flix: Flix): (SyntaxTree.Root, List[CompilationMessage])
+   ```
+
+   It depends only on the lexical/syntactic layer (`Token`, `Source`, `SyntaxTree`,
+   `SourceLocation`) plus an `implicit flix: Flix` context — **not** on `TypedAst`, the
+   JVM backend, or the effect solver. The front-end we need is `Lexer` + `Parser2` and
+   their `ast` support, not the whole compiler.
+
+2. **Byte-losslessness comes from the tokens, not the tree shape.** `SyntaxTree` is
+   deliberately *error-tolerant*: `Tree(kind: TreeKind, children: Array[Child], loc:
+   SourceLocation)` where `Child` is `Tree | Token`, and its own docs warn that a node is
+   **not** guaranteed to have a specific child or a specific number of children. It is
+   therefore not a structurally strict CST. Losslessness instead rests on `SyntaxTree.Root`
+   holding `tokens: Map[Source, Array[Token]]` — every token with its `SourceLocation` —
+   combined with the original source text: whitespace and comments are recovered from the
+   offset gaps between adjacent tokens. That is precisely OpenRewrite's model (prefixes
+   reconstructed from source spans), so parse → print byte equality is achievable; the
+   mechanism is span-based recovery, not a faithful CST.
+
+3. **We must write the printer ourselves.** Flix's own pretty-printer is a stub:
+   `PrettyPrinter.format` currently returns `""`
+   ([source](https://github.com/flix/flix/blob/master/main/src/ca/uwaterloo/flix/tools/fmt/PrettyPrinter.scala),
+   with a comment that the real implementation lands in a follow-up branch). We cannot
+   delegate formatting to Flix; a hand-written `FlixPrinter` is required, exactly as
+   `rewrite-scala` writes its own.
+
+4. **Flix is delivered as a vendored fat JAR, pinned by commit.** There is no usable Flix
+   compiler artifact on Maven Central (a `g:ca.uwaterloo.flix AND a:flix` search returns
+   zero results; the only `*:flix` coordinate, `com.paulbutcher:flix`, is self-labeled "do
+   not use"; publishing is an open upstream discussion,
+   [flix/flix#4380](https://github.com/flix/flix/issues/4380)). Instead, this work consumes
+   a **vendored build of the fork**, produced by
+   [`wstein/java2kotlin-vendor-artifacts`](https://github.com/wstein/java2kotlin-vendor-artifacts),
+   which tags the fork at a commit and publishes `flix-vendor-<version>.jar` as a
+   SHA256-verified GitHub Release asset (alongside an `rewrite-m2-*.tar.gz` bundle of this
+   very `rewrite-fork`). The current release is `vendor-2026.07.20.1`
+   (`flixCommit 1081f92b…`, `rewriteCommit dc7f0d4…`). Inspection of that jar shows it is a
+   **fat, unshaded** artifact: 15,762 classes bundling **Scala 2.13.18**, `fastparse`,
+   `json4s`, `coursier`, and `scopt` at their original package coordinates, with the
+   front-end entry points (`Lexer`, `Parser2`, `Weeder2`, `Token`, `api.Flix`) present. It
+   is *not* a slim parser artifact, and its unshaded `scala.*` (Scala 2.13) namespace would
+   clash with `rewrite-scala`'s Scala 3 on OpenRewrite's shared classpath. This shapes the
+   integration decision below.
+
+## Decision
+
+### Build `rewrite-flix`, incrementally, reusing `J.*` where valid
+
+Follow the `rewrite-scala` shape: a `Flix.CompilationUnit` `SourceFile` whose `printer(...)`
+returns a hand-written `FlixPrinter`; a `FlixParser` that enforces parse → print byte
+equality; a `FlixVisitor`/`FlixIsoVisitor` pair; and a parse → print corpus. `J.*` reuse
+is **narrower than for Scala**: with no OOP model, the class-based `J.*` nodes
+(`J.ClassDeclaration` for OOP classes, inheritance, member access on `this`) do not apply,
+and reuse is limited to the genuinely shared functional surface — identifiers, literals,
+function application, and common expression shapes. Everything Flix-specific —
+declarations (`def`, `enum`, `trait`, `instance`, `mod`), effects, pattern matching, and
+logic/fixpoint constructs — is modeled with `Flix.*` nodes and markers rather than forced
+into Java shapes. Per this repository's first CRITICAL PRINCIPLE,
+**no construct is ever regressed to `J.Unknown`** to make progress; unimplemented syntax
+blocks a phase rather than degrading its type.
+
+### How the Flix parser is obtained (decided: a slim parser artifact)
+
+**Decision:** the vendor pipeline
+([`wstein/java2kotlin-vendor-artifacts`](https://github.com/wstein/java2kotlin-vendor-artifacts))
+publishes a **slim parser artifact** alongside the existing fat `flix-vendor-*.jar`, and
+`rewrite-flix` depends on that slim jar. This keeps `rewrite-flix` a plain in-process
+dependency (no RPC subprocess) carrying only the front-end, not the whole compiler. The
+alternatives considered — loading the whole fat jar through a dedicated isolating
+classloader, or running the parser out-of-process over Rewrite RPC — remain documented
+fallbacks if the slim artifact proves impractical, but are not the chosen path.
+
+Note that slimming is **orthogonal to the Scala-version collision**: the slim jar still
+bundles Scala 2.13, which shares the `scala.*` namespace with `rewrite-scala`'s Scala 3.
+Removing the backend shrinks the jar and its risk surface but does *not* by itself resolve
+that clash — the vendor build must additionally **shade** (relocate `scala.*` and the
+retained third-party packages under a private prefix), or `rewrite-flix` must load the slim
+jar through an isolating classloader. The recommended end state is *slim + shaded*.
+
+**What "slim" requires — a measured constraint.** The front-end cannot be slimmed by simply
+shrinking the fat jar. `Lexer` and `Parser2` use the `ca.uwaterloo.flix.api.Flix`
+god-object *only* through `flix.phaseNew("…"){ … }` (a phase-timing wrapper) and, in
+`Lexer.fuzz`, `flix.options` — but because their compiled classes reference the `Flix`
+type, and `Flix` statically wires every compiler phase (including the JVM backend), the
+class-level closure from `Lexer` + `Parser2` reaches **6,001 of 7,238 Flix classes — the
+same set as `Flix` alone** (measured with `jdeps` on `flix-vendor-2026.07.20.1.jar`, and it
+includes backend classes such as `Eraser`, `Reducer`, and `jvm.AsmOps`). Two ways to
+actually produce a slim jar:
+
+* **(A1) Source decoupling in the flix fork** — remove `Flix` from the front-end *entry
+  points* so the parser runs without a compiler instance: drop `(implicit flix: Flix)` from
+  `Lexer.run`/`Parser2.run` (and dead `fuzz`), inline the `flix.phaseNew(…){…}` timing
+  wrapper, and replace `ParOps.parMap*` (which need `flix.options`) with sequential `.map`
+  (one file at a time). Callers in `Flix.check()` pass `flix` implicitly, so they need no
+  change.
+* **(A2) Method-level shrinking (R8)** — seed R8 at the decoupled entry points and let
+  dead-method elimination drop `Flix.compile()` and the backend it reaches (never called
+  from `Parser2.run`). This is what actually removes the bulk. R8 is chosen over ProGuard
+  for tighter output; both were tried in the spike.
+
+**A1 and A2 are complementary, not either/or** — this is the corrected finding from the
+spike below. A1 alone does *not* shrink the static class graph: even with `Lexer`/`Parser2`
+decoupled, **78 other front-end classes** (`ast.Symbol`, `errors.TypeError`, `Scheme`, …)
+still reference `Flix` for convenience methods, so `jdeps`' conservative class-level closure
+stays at 6,001. But those `Flix`-using methods are never *called* on the parse path, so they
+never load at runtime and A2 prunes them. A1 is the enabler (the parser runs Flix-free); A2
+is the slimmer; **shading** then resolves the Scala clash.
+
+#### Spike results (2026-07-24, verified locally)
+
+Built `wstein/flix-fork@feature/java2kotlin` with `./mill flix.assembly`, applied the A1
+decoupling (2 files: `Lexer.scala`, `Parser2.scala`), and drove `Lexer.run` + `Parser2.run`
+from a standalone object **with no `Flix` instance in scope**:
+
+* Compiles clean under `-Xfatal-warnings`; `Parser2`/`Lexer` bytecode has **zero** references
+  to `ca.uwaterloo.flix.api.Flix`.
+* The parser runs: a sample with a comment, an effect signature, a `let`, and a string
+  interpolation lexed to 24 tokens with **0 lex / 0 parse errors** and one CST unit.
+* **Byte-exact round-trip** reconstructed the source from token offsets + inter-token gaps
+  (comments arrive as `CommentLine` tokens) — losslessness confirmed.
+* `-verbose:class` shows **25 Flix classes loaded and zero backend/`Flix` classes**
+  (no `jvm.*`, `Typer`, `Resolver`, `api.Flix`) — confirming method-level shrinking prunes
+  the backend safely.
+* **R8** (`--classfile` mode, keep rules seeded at `Lexer`/`Parser2` + the `SyntaxTree`/
+  `Token` API) shrank the decoupled jar from **32 MB → 3.4 MB** (15,762 → 1,926 classes):
+  848 Flix classes (the genuine parser closure across all syntax paths), 1,032 Scala, the
+  rest small deps. The parser still round-trips byte-for-byte, and **every backend and
+  `Flix` class is gone**. (ProGuard 7.9.1 with the same rules gave 4.3 MB / 2,432 classes,
+  leaving a residual `Flix$`; R8 is chosen for its tighter output and optimization.)
+* The 1,032 Scala 2.13 classes remain — so **shading is still required** (§ decision) before
+  `rewrite-flix` can share a classpath with `rewrite-scala`.
+
+The remaining work to *Accepted*: apply the A1 decoupling on the fork, add the R8 shrink +
+shading to the vendor build so it emits `flix-parser-<version>.jar`, and pin `rewrite-flix`
+to it. The fork and its build are Apache-2.0, so vendoring is license-compatible; the pin
+(vendor tag + `flixCommit` + SHA256) and license note are recorded in `build.gradle`.
+
+### Phased roadmap
+
+Each phase has a verifiable outcome and does not regress prior phases:
+
+0. **Slim-artifact spike** — ✅ done locally (see "Spike results"): A1 decoupling verified,
+   parser runs Flix-free, byte-exact round-trip, zero backend loaded.
+1. **A1 as a fork PR** — land the `Lexer`/`Parser2` decoupling on
+   `wstein/flix-fork@feature/java2kotlin`.
+2. **Vendor build emits the slim, shaded jar** — `java2kotlin-vendor-artifacts` adds an
+   R8 shrink + shade step and publishes `flix-parser-<version>.jar` next to the fat jar,
+   checksummed and released the same way.
+3. **Module skeleton** — `rewrite-flix` in `settings.gradle`; `build.gradle` that resolves
+   the slim `flix-parser-<version>.jar` from the vendor Release (pinned by tag + SHA256); a
+   minimal `Flix.CompilationUnit`; `FlixParser` wired to `requirePrintEqualsInput`;
+   `FlixVisitor`/`FlixPrinter`; package docs.
+4. **Lossless core** — declarations, expressions, patterns, types, comments, whitespace;
+   parse → print byte equality on a representative corpus.
+5. **Flix-specific constructs** — effects, traits, enums, modules, logic/fixpoint; `Flix.*`
+   nodes and markers as needed.
+6. **Type attribution** — a Flix type mapping mirroring `ScalaTypeMapping`.
+7. **Recipes, style, and canonical formatting** — only after the printer is complete.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* The parser/printer is a substantial, `rewrite-scala`-scale effort and is delivered in
+  the phases above; no phase ships subset support that silently degrades other syntax to
+  `J.Unknown`.
+* Formatting cannot be delegated to Flix while `PrettyPrinter.format` is a stub; the
+  `FlixPrinter` owns all output and is validated by byte-equality round-trips.
+* The module depends on an internal, unstable Flix front-end API (`Lexer`, `Parser2`,
+  `SyntaxTree`) delivered as a slim vendor artifact pinned to a specific release by vendor
+  tag, `flixCommit`, and SHA256. Upgrading the pin is a deliberate, tested step recorded in
+  `build.gradle`.
+* Producing the slim jar adds a shrink + shade step to the vendor pipeline and an A1
+  decoupling patch carried on the flix fork's `feature/java2kotlin` branch. The patch is
+  small (two files) but must be re-applied (or upstreamed) across Flix upgrades — a known,
+  bounded maintenance cost.
+* Slimming and the Scala clash are separate concerns: the slim jar still bundles Scala 2.13,
+  so the vendor build must **shade** it (relocate `scala.*` + retained third-party under a
+  private prefix) for `rewrite-flix` to coexist with `rewrite-scala`'s Scala 3 on one
+  classpath. Whole-fat-jar-plus-classloader-isolation and RPC remain fallbacks without
+  changing the LST or printer.
+* If upstream publishes a real Flix parser library (per flix/flix#4380) or ships a working
+  `PrettyPrinter`, the integration and printer decisions here should be revisited.
+* The integration mechanism is validated (spike); this ADR stays *Proposed* until A1 lands
+  on the fork and the vendor build emits the slim, shaded jar, at which point it and the
+  first `rewrite-flix` code move to *Accepted*.
